S-3 (voice call ×4, 2026-10-28; SUPERSEDES the older text below where they differ): (1) SPEAK-BACK IS ALWAYS ON: the `speakReplies` setting, its toggle row ×4, its tray and rail item and voice-call.json's `speakOff` reason are gone (the `speak_replies` column stays as a legacy shim: `voice.get` answers true to old clients, `voice.update` ignores it). `shouldSpeak` reads context `voiceTurn` in its place: true while a call runs with the voice agent (voice-call.json) or while a push-to-talk / wake turn waits for or plays its reply (the capsule is Thinking or Speaking), so a TYPED message is never read aloud. The voice device's doctor rows `speech` (and `wake`, below) are reported whenever this device is the member's voice device. (2) PUSH TO TALK = A KEY BINDING: the Push to talk toggle and the fixed `shortcuts` list are gone; NO KEY BOUND (`pttShortcut` empty, the new default) = push to talk off (`push_to_talk` stays as a legacy shim: `voice.get` answers `pttShortcut !== ''`; an old client's pushToTalk false clears the key, true with no key binds `ctrl+space`; a migration empties pttShortcut where push_to_talk was false). `pttShortcut` follows `shortcutGrammar`; `shortcutCanonical(text)` (`shortcutParseCases`: `value` = the canonical text or null when the grammar refuses it, `label` = `shortcutLabel(value)`, `copy.shortcutNone` for empty) and `voice.update` refuses any text whose canonical form is not itself (BAD_REQUEST). `shortcutLabel` = each part's `shortcutGrammar.labels` entry (a letter upper case, f13 = F13, mouseN = `labels.mouse` with {n}) joined by `separator`. The row: Settings → Voice's second group keeps ONE row `copy.pushToTalk` (testId `shortcut`) whose value is the binding's label as keycaps (`copy.shortcutNone` while empty). On the IDE of the voice device itself it is THE recorder: a click starts recording (`copy.shortcutRecord` as the placeholder, the held modifiers as `pending`), `captureStep(state, event)` folds the key events (`captureCases`: events `down {key}` / `up {key}` with the grammar's key names plus `escape`, `mouse {button}`; result `status` recording | done | cancelled, `value` the binding after the events, `pending` = the held modifiers' labels + ` + …` (empty while none), `error` = `pttCopy.shortcutNeedsModifier` inline under the row, feedback-states.json `errors`): a non-modifier key with the held modifiers records (canonical order), a bare key outside `bareKeys` shows the error and keeps recording, Esc alone cancels (the binding stays), Backspace or Delete alone clears it (= off), a modifier pressed and released alone records nothing, a left or right click is no binding, a key the grammar does not know is ignored; while recording the IDE releases its own grab so the old binding cannot fire; the clear button (`copy.shortcutClear`, testId `shortcutClear`) empties it too; a done value is written with `voice.update` optimistically (a refusal reverts and toasts). On web, iOS, Android and another desktop the row is READ-ONLY (the label, no picker): keys are recorded on the voice device. The tray's and rail's Push to talk item is no longer a check: while a key is bound it is the action `pushToTalk` (label `copy.pushToTalk` + ` · ` + the label or `shortcutUnavailable`) that opens Settings → Voice; no key = no item. `clearOnNone` clears only wakeWord. `micAvailable` = a key bound or the wake word, and the worker up. `shortcutSupport` reads any grammar value (a `mouseN` part decides as before, with or without modifiers). The recorder hears the mouse buttons the windowing layer reports (gpui: 3-5), and Windows grabs only mouse3-mouse5 (`shortcutReason` mouse for 6-9); mouse6-mouse9 stay valid grammar for X11. The keycaps are THE eUI `Kbd` ×4 (one cap per label part, `KbdGroup`). (3) WAKE DETAIL ×4: the Wake word row's trailing detail says why it is or is not listening on EVERY client: `wakeDetail(context)` (`wakeDetailCases`; context {wakeWord, agent (one picked), online (the voice device), device (its name), state}), in order: null while wakeWord is off; `pttCopy.wakeDetail.noAgent` without an agent; `offline` ({device}) while the voice device is offline; else by `state`: listening, muted (the tray's Mute), downloading, micBusy (a call holds it), meeting, noMicrophone, notGranted, unavailable; null state = `starting`. On the voice device's own IDE `state` is the worker's (`WakeListening` and its reason, the tray's Mute, the call, the meeting); every other client reads the voice device's doctor row `wake` (group voice, reported while wakeWord is on: state ok while listening else off, detail = the device's own `wakeDetail` text, shown verbatim). (4) TRAY: while a call runs on this device (context `inCall`) the Call item reads `copy.trayEndCall` (id `endCall`, always enabled) and ends it. NEW-67 (voice plan v3, V1): THE Settings → Voice section ×4 and the spoken-reply rules (TS reference packages/etalk/src/voice.ts; desktop domain::voice; iOS ExpCore Voice.swift and Android domain/Voice.kt mirror `copy`, `testIds`, `shortcuts` and the option builders). STORAGE: ONE row per member, `user_voice_settings` (server-only table, no shape): voiceDeviceId (a `devices.device_id` of the member's own desktop), agentId (an agent of one of the member's teams), speakReplies, pushToTalk, pttShortcut (one of `shortcuts`), wakeWord, wakePhrase (empty = `Hey {agent}`), language (one of `languages`: the language replies are spoken in), voiceFile (the path of a reference WAV ON the voice device, empty = the built-in voice) and voiceTranscript (what that clip says) (#NEW-73); read with tRPC `voice.get` (missing row = the defaults below), written with `voice.update` (the member only; an unknown device or agent is refused), and handed to the member's devices on every heartbeat (`voice`), with a nudge to the old and new voice device on each write. The per-device `launch_defaults.voice` of NEW-53 is migrated into it and retired. UI: Settings → Personal gains `copy.group` (icon concept `settings-voice`) after Notifications, on web, the IDE, iOS and Android; Device settings no longer has a Voice group. The page = ONE group: row `copy.voiceDevice` = THE device picker over `voiceDeviceOptions` (None first, then the member's desktop devices by name; phones and servers are never a voice device), row `copy.agent` = THE picker over `agentOptions` (None first, the member's agents by label, `{name} · {team}` on a shared name), toggle row `copy.speakReplies`, picker row `copy.language` over `languages` (the row's value AND each menu option read `languageLabel(value, {device})` = the language's label, plus ` · ` and `languageNote(value, {device})` when that is not null: every language is spoken on the voice device's GPU only, so each one notes it, and without one replies are shown, never spoken; no note while no voice device is picked); while a voice device is picked two input rows follow in the same group, `copy.voiceFile` (placeholder `copy.voiceFilePlaceholder`) and `copy.voiceTranscript` (placeholder `copy.voiceTranscriptPlaceholder`), both one line under THE input rule (INPUTS below), at most `limits.voiceFile` / `limits.voiceTranscript`. VOICES (#NEW-74, owner decision 2026-10-26 on #NEW-9): ONE engine speaks English and German, Qwen3-TTS 0.6B Base through CrispASR, zero-shot, F16, on the voice device's GPU only (Kokoro on the CPU is retired); the model downloads on first use (pinned + sha256, never in the binary). Every reply is cloned from the member's reference clip (`voiceFile`, 8-15 s of calm, clean speech) plus its transcript (`voiceTranscript`) for the picked language, or from a built-in reference clip per language while the file is empty: no training, no upload, the file never leaves the voice device. `voices` = the languages the device's speech worker reports: both with a usable GPU, none (`[]`) without one; without a usable GPU on the voice device replies are shown, never spoken, in either language. While a voice device is picked a second group follows under the header `copy.trayHeader` with {device} = the device's name: toggle `copy.pushToTalk`, picker row `copy.shortcut` over `shortcuts`, toggle `copy.wakeWord`, input row `copy.wakePhrase` (placeholder `copy.wakePhrasePlaceholder` with {agent}; THE input rule, at most `limits.wakePhrase`). TOGGLES: every switch reads off and is disabled while the voice device or the agent is None; choosing None for either clears speakReplies, pushToTalk and wakeWord, so picking again never turns listening or speaking on by itself (`clearOnNone`). Push to talk and the wake word are stored now and used from V2/V3/V7. SPEAKING (desktop): `shouldSpeak` decides whether a synced `messages` row is spoken: author_kind `agent`, no card, non-blank body, no author_session_id (a child's post is not the assistant talking), the row belongs to the member's conversation session with the voice agent (`agentSessionId`), speakReplies on, THIS device is the member's voice device (`isVoiceDevice`), the settings' `language` is one THIS device's speech worker reports (`voices`, empty without a usable GPU), and created at or after the moment the watcher armed (a backfill is never read aloud). The text spoken is `spokenText(body, maxChars, language)` (an unknown language reads as `en`): Markdown reduced to what a voice can say, in order: fenced code blocks and tables are dropped; images are dropped; a link keeps its text; a bare URL becomes `spokenWords[language].link`; inline code, emphasis, strike, heading and quote markers are unwrapped; list bullets and numbers drop; a mention `@local@domain` keeps `local`; an issue ref `#EXP-12` loses the `#`; an identifier `ABC-123` is spelled letter by letter and its number read the way people say issue numbers (`identifierNumberWords`: 1-3 digits as a cardinal, 4 digits as two pairs with `hundred` for a trailing 00 and `oh` for a leading 0 in the second pair, `x000` as a cardinal, 5+ digits digit by digit), an all-caps word of 2-5 letters is spelled letter by letter; any other number becomes cardinal words in the language (`numberWords`: integers up to 999,999,999, longer digit by digit, a decimal reads `spokenWords[language].point` then each digit, `%` reads `spokenWords[language].percent`). GERMAN (`de`): cardinals are written German compounds, lowercase (`null`, `eins` standalone, `einundzwanzig`, `einhunderteins`, `eintausenddreihundertneunundsechzig`, `eine Million`, `zwei Millionen fünfhunderttausend`), decimal digits read one by one (`drei Komma eins vier`); issue numbers keep the English shape (`zwölf zweiundvierzig`, `zwölfhundert`, `zwölf null fünf`, `zweitausend`, 5+ digits digit by digit); spelling stays letter by letter and the Markdown rules are the same in every language; whitespace collapses; the result stops at the last sentence end within `maxChars` (else at a word boundary + `copy.ellipsis`). While a reply is spoken the session shows a Dock banner (dock.json `Banner`: icon `media-volume-up`, label `copy.speaking`, title = the spoken text's first sentence, action `copy.stop`, tone muted); Stop ends the voice. While the voice model downloads the toggle row's trailing detail reads `downloadProgress(received, total)`: `copy.downloading` while the total is unknown (0), else `copy.downloadingProgress` with each size in decimal units, MB (no decimal) below 1 GB, else GB with one decimal; received rounds down so it never overstates progress, the total rounds to nearest; a failed download is a toast `copy.downloadFailed` and the switch stays on; the worker retries it with backoff (1 min doubling to 1 h), never on every reply. A worker that keeps crashing is restarted with backoff (2, 4, 8 s) and given up on after 3 crashes in a row: a toast `copy.unavailable`, no more speaking until the setting changes. Speaking stops when the agent or the voice device changes, the setting turns off, or the account changes or signs out (which also ends the worker). TRAY (#NEW-68, voice plan V2): the IDE shows a system-tray item ONLY while THIS device is the member's voice device (Linux: our own StatusNotifierItem + dbusmenu over D-Bus, no GTK, re-registering whenever a StatusNotifierWatcher appears or a host registers, and rechecking when a host unregisters (#NEW-86, so a lost host is noticed at once), so GNOME without the AppIndicator extension shows nothing; macOS and Windows: the native tray), icon = the app icon, and its OS-native menu is `trayMenu(settings, {agent, muted, callAvailable, micAvailable, deviceIsVoiceDevice, screenMemory})` (null = no tray): action `copy.trayOpen` (brings an IDE window up, a new one when none is open; also what clicking the icon does on Linux and Windows), then `copy.trayCall` with {agent} (only while callAvailable: the call lands in V4), a separator; check items `copy.speakReplies`, `copy.pushToTalk` + ` · ` + the shortcut's label, `copy.wakeWord` + ` · ` + the wake phrase (empty = `wakePhrasePlaceholder(agent)`, `…` for no agent), each checked = its stored value and disabled (and unchecked) while the voice device or the agent is None, exactly as on the page; then (#NEW-58, screen-memory.json) the check item Screen memory while `screenMemory.available` (this IDE captures here; absent = no row): label = screen-memory.json `copy.tray`, plus ` · ` + its `copy.paused` while on and `screenMemory.paused` (a denylisted window is focused, the focus is unknown, or the pause hotkey holds it), checked = `screenMemory.on`, always enabled (device-local, never synced, default off, kept across restarts like Mute; turning it off, signing out, another voice device or account deletes the buffer); then `copy.trayMute` only while micAvailable (V3 listens; device-local, never synced, always enabled; #NEW-86: the voice device keeps it across restarts); a separator; actions `copy.traySettings` (opens Settings → Voice) and `copy.trayQuit`. A toggle writes `voice.update` optimistically like the page (the menu flips at once, the stored value is handed to the speaker, a refusal reverts and toasts). While the tray is registered with a host, closing the last window keeps the IDE running (Linux and Windows quit otherwise; macOS always keeps running), so the speech worker stays resident; a lost tray host with no window open brings a window back, and launching the IDE again while it runs brings a window up. PUSH TO TALK (#NEW-54, voice plan V3; its words are `pttCopy`, desktop-only, so the phones' `copy` mirrors stay as they are): only on the member's voice device with pushToTalk on (after `clearOnNone`) does the IDE hold the shortcut. SHORTCUTS: `shortcutSupport(os, session, shortcut, portal)` (`shortcutSupportCases`): Windows and X11 grab every shortcut globally (X11: XGrabKey + XGrabButton, press and release; Windows: RegisterHotKey + release detection, mouse buttons through a low-level mouse hook), macOS every key (Carbon; `ctrl+space` collides with Select previous input source), never a mouse button; Wayland asks the xdg GlobalShortcuts portal (`portal`: KDE 5.27+, GNOME 48+, Hyprland; Activated/Deactivated = hold; the compositor may rebind it, so its `trigger_description` labels the shortcut) and without one the key works only while an IDE window is focused (`focused-only`), never a mouse button. `shortcutOptions(os, session)` = the Shortcut picker's options on the voice device: every `shortcuts` entry whose support is not `unavailable` (`shortcutOptionsCases`; mouse buttons hidden on macOS and Wayland). A shortcut that can't be grabbed never fails silently: the tray's Push to talk item reads `copy.pushToTalk` + ` · ` + `pttCopy.shortcutUnavailable` ({shortcut} = its label), Settings → Voice shows `shortcutReason(reason, shortcut)` inline under the Shortcut row (`pttCopy.shortcutReasons`: taken = another app holds it, noPortal = no portal, declined = the portal refused, mouse = a mouse button where none can be grabbed; `shortcutReasonCases`), and the key still works while an IDE window is focused. FLOW: `pttStep(state, event)` folds key and worker events into the overlay (`pttOverlay(state, agent)`; null = hidden; `pttFlowCases`, events in order from hidden): keyDown{muted} = Listening (Listen, which stops any speech: barge-in) or, muted, `pttCopy.overlayMuted` with `pttCopy.overlayMutedLine` and pill `pttCopy.overlayUnmute` (the microphone never opens); partial = the line, quoted “…”; keyUp = EndListen (the state waits for the worker); heard = `utteranceText` (trimmed; blank = hidden, nothing sent) quoted under `pttCopy.overlayHeard`, the wave thinking; empty = hidden; listenFailed{reason} = `pttCopy.listenFailed[reason]`; sent = `pttCopy.overlayThinking` until the agent's reply row lands; sendFailed = `pttCopy.overlayNotSent` with `pttCopy.overlayNotSentLine` (the text goes into that chat's composer draft); replied{body, speaking} (only while Thinking) = the first sentence of `spokenText(body)` under `copy.speaking` with the primary pill `copy.stop` while Speak replies reads it, else under `pttCopy.overlayReplied`; speakFinished = `pttCopy.overlayReplied`; cancel (sign-out, a voice-device change, push to talk off, another agent or language: the host sends CancelListen) and hide = hidden. The pill is the agent's name (`…` without one) unless named above. `overlayHideAfterMs` = how long a state stays before it fades (absent = until the next event). UTTERANCE (`utteranceCases`): `utteranceInput(heard, {teamId, agentId, conversationId})` = `sessions.send` {sessionId, text} into the member's conversation with the agent, or {teamId, agentId, text} while there is none yet; null for blank text or no agent: a plain message, no marker. TRAY (V3): `micAvailable` = push to talk or (#NEW-56) the wake word here and the speech worker up; context `shortcutUnavailable` and `shortcutLabel` (the portal's trigger description) shape the Push to talk item. OVERLAY: a transparent, always-on-top, never-focused window at the bottom centre of the display under the pointer, 24 px above its edge (Wayland: the compositor places it), hosting THE capsule; `overlaySpecimens` are the styleguide `voice-call-overlay` rows ×2 (web + desktop read them). WAKE WORD (#NEW-56, voice plan V7; desktop-only like push to talk, no new UI: the tray's Wake word item and Settings → Voice's two rows are the whole surface): only on the member's voice device with wakeWord on (after `clearOnNone`) and the tray's Mute off does the IDE hand its speech worker the phrase (`wakePhrase`, empty = `wakePhrasePlaceholder(agent)`; never while the agent's name is unknown) and the language; Mute, Wake word off, another device, agent or account takes it back and cancels a wake turn in flight. The worker keeps the microphone open and matches the phrase without a model of its own (talk-listen.json `wake`); a heard phrase is a keyDown{muted: false} for one turn (`woke`: Listening, Speak replies stops: barge-in), the worker ends the turn itself with heard or empty, and from there the flow is push to talk's (`pttFlowCases`). A push-to-talk key-down replaces a wake turn. A CALL TAKES PRECEDENCE (voice-call.json, talk-listen.json `micOwnerCases`): Call closes the wake word's microphone (a wake turn in flight ends unanswered), the wake scan pauses for the whole call (no wake match, the tray dot goes out), and it comes back after Hangup; a push-to-talk Listen during a call is refused. ALWAYS-ON MICROPHONE: while the wake word holds the microphone open the tray icon says so, `trayIcon(context)` (`trayIconCases`): null = no tray (not the voice device), `listening` = the app icon with a filled dot in its lower right corner while `wakeListening` (the worker reported the microphone open) and not muted, OR while `meetingListening` (#NEW-57: a meeting runs on this device, the worker reported its channels listening and Pause listening does not hold it; Mute microphone never pauses a meeting, so muted keeps that dot: the icon never hides an open microphone), else `app`; #FEED-163: `recording` wins over both whenever `meetingRunning` (a meeting runs on this device, paused or not, for its WHOLE run): the app icon with a RED record dot in the same corner (the destructive token's red, never templated or tinted by the OS, so it reads as recording on a light or dark macOS menu bar, the Windows notification area and a Linux StatusNotifierItem alike), the one sign a room is being transcribed. `meetingRunning` absent = false. WAKE PHRASE LENGTH (#NEW-56 review of #1263): a stored wake phrase needs at least `limits.wakePhraseMinLetters` LETTERS (letters only: spaces, digits and punctuation do not count; `Jürgen` = 6), so a short word like `Ok` can't fire on every segment; an empty phrase stays valid (it means `wakePhrasePlaceholder(agent)`). `wakePhraseError(text)` (`wakePhraseErrorCases`) = `copy.wakePhraseTooShort` for a trimmed, non-empty text with fewer letters, else null. `voice.update` refuses such a `wakePhrase` with that text (BAD_REQUEST), and the IDE never listens for one stored before the rule; Settings → Voice on web, the IDE, iOS and Android checks it when the Wake phrase field is left or submitted: an invalid phrase is not sent (the stored one stays) and the line shows inline under the field (feedback-states.json `errors`: the field's red border + the 13px rose line, never a toast) until the next edit. LISTENING DETAIL (#NEW-86; a tray host is not always there, GNOME without AppIndicator shows none, so the page says it too): in the IDE's Settings → Voice on the voice device itself the Wake word toggle row's trailing detail (the Speak replies row's download-progress slot) reads `wakeDetail(context)` (`wakeDetailCases`, desktop only: the phones and web never know whether the device's microphone is open): null while `here` is false (another device, or the styleguide twin) or wakeWord is off, `pttCopy.overlayMuted` while the tray's Mute is on, `pttCopy.overlayListening` while `wakeListening` (the worker reported the wake word's microphone open), else null (downloading, no microphone, a call holds it). No new words, no new component. RAIL VOICE (#NEW-97, approved 2026-10-27; desktop only): a tray host is not always there (GNOME without AppIndicator), so while NO host shows the tray the IDE rail's footer carries a voice button, `railVoice(settings, context)` (`railVoiceCases`; context = trayMenu's plus `wakeListening` and `trayHosted`, the tray's own registered state; null = no button): only while THIS device is the voice device, wakeWord is on (after `clearOnNone`) OR a meeting runs (`meeting.on`, #NEW-57: without a tray host it is the only place a running meeting shows and stops) and `trayHosted` is false. The button is the footer's Computer button (the small ghost square) with the `settings-voice` glyph; `badge` = the rail's dot in `destructive` exactly while `trayIcon(context)` is `listening`; `tooltip` = while a meeting runs the tray's Meeting mode row label (`Meeting mode · {who}`, paused or not), else `pttCopy.overlayMuted` while muted, else `pttCopy.railListening` with {phrase} = the Wake word row's phrase; context adds `meetingListening` (trayIcon's); `menu` = THE pointer menu of `trayMenu(settings, context)`'s rows minus Open, Quit and the separators (a pointer menu has no dividers), each running the tray's own handler (the toggles optimistic, Mute and Screen memory device-local and kept). #NEW-91: THE synthesis chunks of a spoken reply on the voice device, `speechChunks(spoken, streaming)` (`speechChunkCases`; TS reference, desktop voice crate `speech_chunks`): its sentences, split after `.` `!` `?` followed by a space, trimmed, blanks dropped (a decimal point is no end). `streaming` = the speaker hands out audio while it still synthesizes (Qwen3-TTS's own streaming entry point, the Linux and macOS runtimes: the first audio after 8 codec frames of any sentence): sentences only, never a clause split (it would only break the prosody). Without it (the Windows runtime, one whole utterance per call) the first sentence's first clause is synthesized on its own: split at the first `,` `;` `:` followed by whitespace, or ` - `, when that leaves 2 to 8 words in front and something behind; only the first mark counts (a `,` or `:` inside a number is none, nor a hyphen); the front keeps its punctuation, a dash is dropped. Target: first audio under 400 ms at p95 on the voice device's GPU (measured with `crates/etalk-engine/examples/call_latency.rs --first-audio`). INPUTS (#NEW-75): THE rule of the page's three one-line inputs (Voice file, Transcript, Wake phrase) ×4, `voiceTextInput(value, max)` (`voiceTextInputCases`; desktop `voice_text_input`, iOS `Voice.textInput`, Android `Voice.textInput`), applied AS YOU TYPE (every edit and paste, so an over-long paste or a tab never reaches the server): first (#FEED-160) every maximal run of consecutive whitespace control characters (tab U+0009, LF U+000A, VT U+000B, FF U+000C, CR U+000D, NEL U+0085) becomes ONE space (`a
b` = `a b`, a pasted line break separates words, never glues them; spaces next to the run are kept, not merged), then every other control character is dropped (Unicode Cc = C0 U+0000-U+001F, DEL U+007F, C1 U+0080-U+009F; dropped, no space: `a�b` = `ab`, and a dropped one between two whitespace controls splits their run, so each side becomes its own space; format characters such as an emoji's ZWJ stay), then the value is cut to the longest prefix of at most `max` UTF-16 code units (zod's `.max`, the server's count), whole code points only (a surrogate pair straddling the cap is dropped whole, never split; a grapheme may be). Leading and trailing spaces stay while typing; the value is trimmed on save (blur, submit, the debounce). `max` = `limits.voiceFile`, `limits.voiceTranscript`, `limits.wakePhrase` (= `voice.update`'s caps; the server refuses Cc and longer text with the same counts). MEETING MODE (#NEW-57, meeting.json): `shouldSpeak` is false while a meeting runs on the voice device (context `meeting`: nothing is read aloud mid-meeting). `trayMenu` context gains `meeting` {available, on, who} and `pause` {available, paused}: after Wake word the check item `meeting.json copy.meeting` (+ ` · ` + who while on; checked = on; enabled like the other toggles), and after Screen memory the check item `meeting.json copy.pause` + ` · ` + `meeting.json pause.label` (only while `pause.available`: a meeting runs or screen memory is on; checked = paused; always enabled); while a meeting runs the Call item is hidden. The rail voice menu mirrors these rows like the others.

shortcutGrammar._: S-3: a push-to-talk binding is ANY key or mouse combination the member presses (recorded like a game keybind), stored canonical: zero or more `mods` in this order joined by `+`, then exactly ONE key: a letter a-z, a digit 0-9, a function key f1-f24, one of `named`, or a mouse button mouse3-mouse9 (`mouse1`/`mouse2` are clicks, never a binding). A key in `bareKeys` (and every mouse button) may stand alone; every other key needs at least one modifier (a bare letter would steal typing). Empty = no key bound = push to talk off. At most `maxLength` characters (the column).
